text:
tara: having bad onboarding vibes. sampleapp generator example doesn't respond to ctx cancel when auth is rotated mid-flight. users hit the tutorial and it just hangs.

simon: ouch. do you have repro steps?

tara: yes: 1) run sampleapp with example token provider that returns a token valid for 10s 2) call generator.Stream until token expiry 3) runtime responds with 401 during an in-flight chunk 4) ctx cancel in app doesn't unblock generator.Next() — goroutine remains.

lee: can you paste the sample loop? we might be missing Close/Cancel calls in the SDK example.

tara: snippet from sampleapp README:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
defer cancel()
g := client.NewGenerator(cfg)
stream := g.Generate(ctx, opts)
for stream.Next() {
  fmt.Print(string(stream.Current()))
}
if err := stream.Err(); err != nil {
  log.Printf("stream finished: %v", err)
}
```

tara: users expect context timeout to cancel mid-stream. Instead the client transport seems to block on a read after the 401 and never sets stream.Err() or returns from Next().

simon: two likely issues: 1) auth 401 arrives but transport swallow/quiet-closes the socket (no error surfaced) 2) Next() is implemented as blocking receive that only wakes on frame but doesn't observe ctx.Done().

lee: agreed. fix options: a) make receive loop select on ctx.Done() and inbound frames b) on seeing 401 control frame, set stream.Err(ErrStreamAuthExpired) and close recv goroutine c) expose stream.CloseWithError(err) so sampleapps can proactively terminate.

tara: I think we should do all three. Exposing CloseWithError is tiny API surface and helps sample apps.

qa: CI caught a flaky test earlier: TestSampleAppTimeoutHang — seems related. devops-bot posted failure logs: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/actions/8567 failed.

simon: I'll open a PR that: - adds ctx select in recv loop - introduces exported ErrStreamAuthExpired - adds stream.CloseWithError(err) - updates sampleapp README to show idiomatic cancellation pattern with errors.Is checks.

lee: for docs, example pattern:```go
for stream.Next() {
  // process chunk
}
if errors.Is(stream.Err(), redwood.ErrStreamAuthExpired) {
  // refresh token and recreate generator or bail with friendly message
}
```

tara: can we also update onboarding quickstart to mention "if you see hang, try calling stream.CloseWithError(err) or context cancel"? new users won't know.

qa: add an integration that simulates an auth rotation mid-stream and asserts that Next() returns false within 2s of ctx cancel. That will catch regressions.

simon: one UX discussion: should we automatically try to reattach the same generator ID after auth refresh? That would be nice but introduces state sync issues (partial responses, local KV). For now, document re-create path.

lee: agreed. file an issue for automatic resume as a follow-up (low priority).

devops-bot: test queue: queued patch/sim/ctx-recv-select (will run integration).

tara: thanks everyone. once PR lands I'll update the tutorial and ping marketing to re-publish the quickstart screenshots so they don't show the old blocking loop.
